work.text: It gives, again, a beautiful effect of sunlight, and the [architectural] details of the church are shown with an exquisite [clearness]. The little figures are lively and interesting
work.lead: Campbell Dodgson on Saint-Étienne-du-Mont, etched in 1852:

work.text: His method was this—First, he made not a sketch but a number of sketches, two or three inches square, of parts of his picture, which he put together and [arranged] into a harmonious whole.

source.author: Francis Seymour Haden
source.title: Quoted in Keppel, Charles Meryon: A Biographical Sketch

moment.text: Nearly every etching in the series reveals technical skill, but even the technical skill is exercised most enthusiastically in those etchings which have the advantage of impressive subjects, and which the collector willingly cherishes for their mysterious suggestiveness or for their pure beauty.

matters.text: In solitary wanderings about the old streets of Paris and meditations in his garret in the Rue St. Etienne-du-Mont, he formed plans for his series of etchings of old Paris and began to make studies for them.
